questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: it was mandatory for my studies

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nice place with good ammenities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UCPH was great for most of it. Kanazawa University sucks

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Hard, There was barely anything written in english and we were told about everything at once, so it was hard to know what was important and what wasn't.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: barely anything, there was one person who could speak english on campus to help us set up our internet. everything else was done in japanese. Except for the endless seminars that told us a river of information of which very little mattered.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They gave us three different pieces of paper that explained how to log in to a website and none that said when we would get our student ID

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different dorm rooms, no notes here. Except for the complete lack of english they were nice.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In the dorms we had a kitchen and there were several cafeterias for lunch

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You need google translate and pray to god you get put in a dorm with some people who speak english.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a system where a japanese student will help you with everything you need. This system did not work in praxis.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was online, though the system was clearly machine translated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Log on to the website, click the modules you want once you find them. If you need to drop out of a module after the registration period, (10 days) you need to go to the office and fill out a form. The teachers cannot do it for you

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was told to go to the office, without anyone saying which one.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was put in a low level language class and was not told how to move up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know what you want before hand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bad teachers, i had language studies with teacher who did not speak more than one language and therefore could not explain anything to us. If we did not know what a word meant we were out of luck.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: We had 90 minuttes of teaching a day, they blazed through the syllabus. They never repeated anything so we just had to learn everything without a chance to repeat it. Moreover we had 4 teachers who did not talk enough to each other so sometimes a teacher would repeat something we had learned yesterday not realizing we had already completed these tests, or they would expect us to know something we had not already learned.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Well i did not learn anything so it was much worse.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Japanse Language
Gender studies
Japanese Thought
Japanese culture through the way of tea

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese culture through the way of tea was pretty fun, we learned a lot about tea ceremonies. Not very academic but it was enjoyable

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay a seperate insurance despite having my own from home. Also everything had to be paid in cash.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The bus fare adds up. If you want to go to Tokyo it costs 500 DKK each way so 1000 DKK total just to go there, it also takes 4 hours by train.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We did not get an actual introduction. There was apparently a group for exchange-students but i was not informed of this at all.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I dont know. 
You could go to parties i guess.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Leave Kanazawa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
if you want to go to Japan dont go here. 
Go to fukuooka or Tokyo

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going home again

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
questions.answer:
I did not enjoy this trip.
I have never wanted to drop out more than when i was in Japan.
You might not be autistic so you could probably enjoy it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
